public_rationale: The Harvey episode illustrates how more usage can increase serving costs. It does not establish that greater demand generally causes larger losses across AI businesses, or that their most engaged customers are generally their least profitable. The reported return to positive gross margins after changes in model use also limits the broader inference. Neither industry-wide causation nor the customer-level ranking is settled by the accessible evidence.
limitations: The claim is assessed as a general pattern rather than a literal universal law.
Gross margin, customer contribution and net losses are different measures.
Secondary reporting about one company cannot establish industry prevalence.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In AI, more demand produces larger losses, and the most engaged customers are the least profitable.

statement.excerpt: In basically any industry, the more demand you have, the more money you make, but in AI, the more demand you get, the more money you lose, and your most engaged customers are also your least-profitable.

from_speaker: the more demand you get, the more money you lose
your most engaged customers are also your least-profitable
our_interpretation: Read this as a claimed general economic pattern among AI service businesses in the surrounding discussion, not merely a claim that some fixed-price plans can lose money.
Demand can rise through more paying customers or through more usage by existing customers; those mechanisms must be distinguished.
Read least-profitable as lowest customer contribution after the costs of serving that customer. Company-wide losses are a separate measure.
Use January–September 2026 as the contextual period: the passage describes Harvey's usage and margin changes during that year through its pre-post recovery.
This is a qualitative causal claim across businesses, not a specified monetary amount for one company.
criteria.support_condition: Representative causal evidence shows that additional demand generally increases AI businesses' losses and that their most engaged customers have the lowest contribution after serving costs, accounting for pricing, model mix and other cost changes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence shows that additional demand generally improves contribution or reduces losses, or that the most engaged customers are not generally the least profitable. Isolated exceptions are insufficient to settle the general pattern.
